items.title: 《巫师 3》开发者谈论过去的歌曲 DLC 详情
items.summary: IGN spoke to CD Projekt Red's level design lead Miles Tost and Songs of the Past writer Paula Meissner at the

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/24/the-witcher-3-gwent-songs-of-the-past-1787611131275.png

It's been more than a decade since The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was first released, but CD Projekt Red isn't quite finished with the game just yet. Songs of the Past , the game's third expansion, is set to arrive in 2027, bringing with it an entirely new region to explore, new monsters to hunt, and more stories to tell.

But how do you expand on a game as beloved as The Witcher 3 without upsetting its notoriously dedicated fans? And how do you keep things fresh while remaining faithful to a universe with decades of established lore?

IGN spoke to CD Projekt Red's level design lead Miles Tost and Songs of the Past writer Paula Meissner at the Lucca Comics & Games festival about creating a distinct new corner of the Continent, the surprising importance of local booze, and why even bringing characters back from the dead doesn't necessarily mean breaking canon.

IGN: Talking about Songs of the Past, from a pure level design perspective, is there a special new mechanical hook that you're looking at for players? And also, how does the environment actively change in a way that maybe veteran players of The Witcher 3 are going to be finding something new?

Miles Tost: Generally speaking, the introduction of a whole new region. And if you've played the base game and the other expansions, for us, these regions are really fun. I think they have a lot of answers for that question by themselves because we try to always make each one feel unique, not just visually, but in the sense of the traversal. Skellig, for example, has a lot of boat travel as a reliance. It's also very mountainous. No Man’s Land is a much wider space. And I think with the value of Lettin, you'll basically see also that as you move around — we're not introducing a new motion mechanic as far as I'm aware — but generally it's really important to us that when you are in an area, you have this distinct feeling of being in this space.

And this goes further culturally, for example. The people of Lettin have their own cultural backdrop. There are some British influences in the aristocracy there, but also we have very, very many Polish countryside influences there. You see that in the architecture, and we usually go pretty deep in thinking about the cultural identity of these spaces. So with Skellig, we have the more Viking-esque influences, but here, these people have their own alcohol.

It's a fun thing to mention because — Bracket is what it's called — it's a kind of fusion between honey and beer. It feels like such a small thing, but for us it's very important, because it draws a lot on what this region is. So for the production of it, you need honey and you need hops. And so you will find both of these in the area. And other than it being a cultural export, of the area and the economical backbone of the place, it even changes how we think about monsters there. So in the demo we've shown, we're basically introducing one new monster, the Swarmion, and these guys love honey. They use hornets as a means of protection, all that stuff. And so the logical reason there is because what kind of monster would live there? So the Swarmion makes sense. So you find that this seemingly small thing of these guys having their own alcohol, and it really has this huge effect on the entire area. And so this is a bit of how we're trying to make things feel unique and special. And it goes into the quest storytelling and all of that.

IGN: Obviously, The Witcher has maybe one of the deepest lores in fiction, with lots of established canon. With Songs of the Past, was there a particular piece of deep lore that was particularly tricky to untangle? And as you were putting all this together, did you have to bend any of the established canon to make the story fit?

Paula Meissner: We actually do have an amazing lore team in CDPR that we are cooperating with. And these guys are just amazing. They know everything, every detail from the books, from every game, from every piece of franchise content. So we do talk with them on a regular basis to make sure that we don't say anything stupid and that we stay actually truthful to the lore. But yeah, it is a tricky question because it touches on topics that weren't revealed yet. So there were definitely challenges, but I don't know how much I can say about those.

Miles Tost: The general thought is that we try to always also evolve and make things fresh. So it's really important for us to not really think in this way of like, “Oh, can we do this or can we not? If we do, how? How would we bring Regis back?" If we just told people before Blood and Wine, "Yeah, we're going to do it." A lot of the hardcore fans would probably go like, "That's impossible. He fucking vaporized. How would he?" And I think we asked ourselves those same questions, and ultimately I think we settled on something that works as an expectation where he's like, "Yeah, he's back, but he's like 10% of his power, and he's still recovering. He's only been able to recover because he's had help from this other higher vampire."

Geralt, by himself, is already like, "Hey, let's just bring him back from the dead." And it works as long as you can explain it and make it make sense. And I think this is really the approach that we're trying to take. So we don't really try to retcon things, but we do try to find cool ways to expand and build on the franchise and the established lore as long as we can find ways to explain it.

Paula Meissner: We often actually use discussing challenges with the lore team as [original Witcher author] Andrzej Sapkowski would do it. If you look at the books and lore of The Witcher in the books, it's such a mix of everything, to be honest. And even if you hear Sapkowski in interviews and people ask him these questions, he's often like “Whatever.” So yeah, this is the ultimate argument that we use sometimes, and sometimes it works.

items.title: 据报道，育碧希望从 Xbox 手中收购 Arkane
items.summary: There might be hope for Arkane after all: A new report says multiple companies have made offers for it.

content.v: A new report from Bloomberg says Dishonored developer Arkane might not be as doomed as it appeared last month, as multiple companies have made offers to acquire the studio.

Citing "people familiar with the negotiations," the Bloomberg report says Ubisoft is among Arkane's suitors, as are at least two other unnamed gaming companies. Xbox has also considered selling the studio to its own management, effectively making it independent, although whether that option is still on the table isn't clear.

Despite producing an enviable slate of acclaimed immersive sims over the years (until it was compelled by senior leadership to do otherwise ), Arkane fell victim to the Xbox "reset" in July that saw thousands of employees laid off (with more still awaiting their fates) and four studios cast adrift. Arkane avoided being the fifth, reportedly thanks to France's "Florange Law" that compelled Xbox to search for a buyer before pulling the plug.

The deadline for that search was November 13, after which Arkane would be shuttered—but a few weeks ahead of that date, Microsoft extended it by a month , to "explore options, including finding a partner to support the studio through the development work still ahead," a reference to the Marvel's Blade game Arkane currently has in development. That extension suggested there was at least some hope that Arkane might find a new home, instead of being closed.

Going from Xbox to Ubisoft could be viewed as a "frying pan to fire" move, given Ubisoft's own ongoing financial struggles, layoffs, and closures . But Arkane's immersive sim expertise could be a good fit for some of Ubisoft's biggest properties, including Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and—yes, I'm just going to say it—Splinter Cell, which would be magnificent in the style of Dishonored. Arkane and Ubisoft both being French companies can't hurt, either.
I've reached out to Xbox and Ubisoft for comment on the report, and will update if I receive a reply.

others.title: 《Control Resonant》是 Remedy 有史以来销售最快的游戏，收入大幅增长

content.v: It's been a good few months for Remedy Entertainment. In its latest financial results , the Finnish game developer announced that its third quarter revenue had more than tripled to €39.6 million ($44.3 million) from the €12.2 million ($13.7 million) it made during the same quarter last year.

That spike in income is all thanks to preorders and launch sales of Control Resonant—of which only the first seven days of sales were counted in Remedy's third quarter figures. On October 15, Resonant sold its millionth copy, making it the fastest-selling game in Remedy history.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/evrRFHYfe4RHsRumRG5eyA-1920-80.jpg

"This is our first self-published game of this scale, built on our own Control IP," said Remedy CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon, who was appointed to the position earlier this year . "Praised by players and critics alike, it marks a defining milestone for the company."

Gaudechon also noted that "close to 50%" of Resonant players were Control newcomers, indicating the sequel had achieved "a key goal" of expanding the audience for Remedy's brand of stylish interdimensional sicko content. Its mission for the immediate future, the CEO said, is to continue delivering Resonant to more interested players—2.4 million of whom still have yet to turn their wishlists into purchases, according to Remedy data.

"Our priority now is to get Control Resonant into the hands of more players. Excellent player reviews, penetration in all our target markets and a substantial outstanding wishlist base give a solid foundation for the game's longer-term sales potential, supported by both organic visibility as well as our targeted marketing activities," Gaudechon said. "As with the launch, we will invest with discipline, prioritizing actions with a clear return."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TQYdAbodP3uRF5Co7X7o2Y-1920-80.jpg

While Remedy's operating profit margin was still thin for the quarter—1.5% of revenue, or €0.6 million—Resonant's strong launch performance is a welcome change of pace from where the studio was at the end of last year. In November 2025, it had posted an operating loss of €16.4 million thanks to the flop of FBC Firebreak. From the sounds of it, Remedy's aiming to continue that momentum with whatever work it has planned next.

"Alongside the launch of Control Resonant, our other projects are proceeding in the pipeline," Gaudechon said. "Sales over the remainder of the year will ultimately define our financial year 2026. Control Resonant gives us a solid foundation for growth."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/6offQUY4CXebir2TC27dMd-1920-80.jpg

items.title: 新娘在《Valorant》中挑战新郎在结婚前击败她后，引起了热议
items.summary: A bride in China is going viral for giving her husband-to-be a wild challenge: making him beat her at Valorant

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/03/bride-goes-viral-groom-valorant-1793741754879.jpg
A bride in China is going viral for giving her husband-to-be a wild challenge: making him beat her at Valorant before they could officially marry.

A video showing the couple facing off in Riot’s tactical first person shooter has racked up nearly three million views in just one day. In the clip, the bride — decked out in her wedding finery and delicate hair ornaments — takes virtual shots at her soon-to-be lawfully wedded opponent, who sits across from her while a group of friends and family look on in amusement.

While this is certainly a unique way to celebrate one’s nuptials, it isn’t totally out of the ordinary. In fact, pre-wedding challenges like these are actually part of Chinese culture. They’re called ‘door games,’ and they’re a playful, lighthearted way to prepare for the actual ceremony and following reception.

Traditionally, these are silly tasks organized by bridesmaids that the groom must successfully complete in order to ‘earn’ the right to actually marry his bride. They usually take place the morning before the wedding at the home of the bride’s family, and his groomsmen are often enlisted to help. It’s a symbolic way of making the groom ‘prove his worth’ before he takes the bride’s hand in marriage.

Door games can be anything the bridesmaids choose, really; according to China Insider, these generally involve tasks like eating unusual foods, athletic challenges like doing push-ups, or testing their knowledge with trivia. In this case, the bridesmaids decided to put his elite gaming skills to the test — and it went so viral that even the official Valorant Instagram account took notice.
“Wait, the wife is lowkey locked in,” it said in a comment.

“The problem is if he wins, she will remember it for life, and he would not hear the end of it, but if he doesn’t, it would be near impossible to find another gem like her,” one viewer joked, while another called it the true definition of “skill-based matchmaking.”
Even the CEO of pro esports team GAM commented, saying, “How do we sign her?”
This is the latest gamer wedding to go viral after a Pokémon fan was able to fund his wedding by selling a trio of rare Charizard cards that had been stored in his attic for a mind-boggling $44,000.
And in 2024, a streamer couple took social media by storm for their Black Ops 6-themed wedding that they held at the Call of Duty Next event in Washington, D.C. Now, that’s true love.

items.title: 这个定制的 Xbox-In-An-Alligator 控制台实际上是 GTA 6 的一个大广告
items.summary: Given that Sony holds the marketing rights for Grand Theft Auto 6 , Microsoft has had to get creative to promo

content.v: Given that Sony holds the marketing rights for Grand Theft Auto 6 , Microsoft has had to get creative to promote the open-world crime game for Xbox--and the company's latest effort in that department goes big.

Say Hello to the X-Bite, a playable Xbox Series X console that was designed to look like it was swallowed whole by one of Florida's millions of alligators. Microsoft only made one of these ornate consoles, and you have to win a contest to get it.

Microsoft's blog post doesn't mention GTA 6 or Rockstar Games, but Xbox marketing boss Josh Munsee said the system has "pure Miami vibes," and that's a pretty obvious reference to GTA 6 given the game takes place in a stand-in, Vice City, for the popular Florida city. The blog post says the winner of the console can play "some of the biggest games of the year" using it, and that's no doubt another nod to GTA 6.

"This November, Xbox is heading to Florida--home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe," Microsoft said in its announcement of the X-Bite.

The X-Bite is about five feet long, and the console itself sits inside the alligator, with the Nexus/Guide button illuminated through the gator's skin. The lucky winner will also get a custom Xbox controller with simulated bite marks on it.
The custom console was designed by creature animatronic specialist John Nolan Studio, which did work for The Witcher and Jurassic World Dominion.

Microsoft's fine print states that the gator console is a "custom fabrication" and wasn't made from a real alligator. "No actual alligators were used or harmed in the making of this console," Microsoft said. The estimated value of the console is $800, Microsoft said.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/GTAGator.jpg?w=636

You can enter for a chance to win the X-Bite by following Xbox on X, Instagram, or TikTok, reposting the sweepstakes post , and then add #XbiteSweepstakes to your repost. You'll also need to have a public account.

The sweepstakes runs now through November 10. The winner, who will be chosen by a random draw, will have 48 hours to respond if they're selected. "Miss the window, and this gator makes a clean getaway," Microsoft said in yet another reference to GTA 6.

GTA 6 is getting special treatment for its PS5 edition, and this has so far included a limited-edition DualSense controller inspired by the game and trailers for GTA 6 that end by telling people the game "plays best" on PS5. The game's recent launch trailer does not include the Xbox logo, either.
GTA 6 is of course not exclusive to Xbox, and there is no evidence that it "plays best" on PS5.

According to Sensor Tower , GTA 6 has sold about 2 million copies so far on Xbox Series X|S, compared to 5.75 million on PS5. Xbox is not worried the PS5 version massively pacing ahead of Xbox, in part because the 74%/26% split in favor of PS5 over Xbox reflects Xbox's current share of the console market . GTA 6 is breaking records already for Xbox, the company has said.

Microsoft takes a 30% cut of games sold on the Xbox platform, so that could end up being a huge number when the game launches, even if it's far behind PS5. At about 2 million copies sold on Xbox so far, according to Sensor Tower, that's $192 million in gross revenue; Xbox's cut would be about $57.6 million. Sensor Tower has said the majority of GTA 6 preorders should come in the final week before release, and could reach 25 million.

If the split stays about where it is now, that would be about 6.5 million units on Xbox by launch, generating more than $170 million in platform fees paid to Xbox. Of course, these are just ballpark estimates, but it's a sure thing that GTA 6 is going to be a big deal for Xbox. Microsoft already alluded to this, as the company forecast major growth for Xbox content and services in the current quarter, and while management didn't attribute this to any particular title, the gargantuan release of GTA 6 is no doubt factored in.
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

content.v: 评论作者回顾了《星球大战：前线3》约二十年来多次启动、又多次取消的历史，并认为所谓系列“诅咒”，实质上是公司决策、内部政治、授权限制与强硬工期反复压倒了项目的开发潜力。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261104/1793740692_482904_jpg_r.jpg
Pandemic Studios于2005年推出《星球大战：前线2》后，曾着手开发后续作品。设计师Dan Nanni回忆称，主机世代转换期间的谈判最终破裂，团队也无法满足LucasArts提出的一年开发期限。
LucasArts随后与Free Radical Design合作开发另一版本。该版本允许玩家从星球地表登船升空，并无缝进入太空战斗。多年后曝光的素材展示了项目规模，部分开发者称其完成度一度达到75%至95%，但游戏最终仍未上市。文章认为，管理层变动、错过项目节点以及缺少内部支持，共同导致这一版本遭到取消。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261104/1793740693_772982_jpg_r.jpg
进入EA时代后，代号“维京计划”、包含开放世界元素的衍生项目也曾进入开发，但团队未能赶上2020年秋季的目标，项目于2019年初终止。
作者还提到，近期有消息称EA与DICE正计划制作《星球大战：前线3》，并将此事与BioWare关闭及另一项目取消联系起来。不过，这些内容目前仍停留在消息层面，尚不能视为正式确认。

items.title: 在 GTA 6 和黑色星期五之前，哪些 PS5 和 Xbox 游戏机有现货？
items.summary: Sony and Microsoft are warning about console shortages ahead of GTA 6 and Black Friday. Which consoles are ava

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/03/untitled-design-1793738170553.png
With both Black Friday and the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 around the corner, console shortages have been in the news lately.

Xbox head Asha Sharma recently said there’s more demand than Xbox consoles available , and Microsoft told Xbox owners to trade in their dusty consoles . Meanwhile, over on the other side of the aisle, Sony wants to buy your PS5 for $400 , and anyone in the market for a PS5 Pro may have to shell out as much as $1,400 to a reseller to get one.

Console stock must be getting pretty dire, right? To answer that question, I visited all the major online retailers to see what the status is surrounding console availability. And what I found was, with the exception of the PS5 Pro, every current model of every current console is widely available at manufacturer-suggested retail price (MSRP).
Featured in this article

Now, that doesn't mean that's how things will stay as GTA 6 and Black Friday creep nearer. And it's worth noting that those MSRPs have gone up in recent years. But at least at this pre-Black Friday, pre-GTA 6 moment in time, it’s not hard to find a new game console at retail price – unless you want a PS5 Pro. Let’s take a look at where things stand with every current model of every game console.
PS5 Pro Is Sold Out

To kick things off, yes, new PlayStation 5 Pro consoles are sold out everywhere. You can still get a used one at eBay or marked up by third-party retailers at some of the links above, but they cost around $1,500, so buy at your own risk. Moving on…
PS5 with Disc Drive

Even though Sony is doing away with discs starting in January 2028 , the PlayStation company will still happily sell you a PS5 with a disc drive. This model of the PS5 is widely available pretty much everywhere, so pick one up at your favorite retailer. It's unlikely these consoles will get discounts during P layStation's Black Friday sale this year .
PS5 Digital Edition

As you may have heard (in the previous blurb), Sony is doing away with discs starting in January 2028. If you’re ready to embrace that digital-only life, feel free to grab this one. At $599.99, it’s pretty much a steal in this (horrible) economy. However, it's worth noting that Amazon and GameStop are currently sold out of new stock of this model, while other retailers have it in stock.
Xbox Series X (with Disc Drive)

The standard Xbox Series X with a disc drive is available at most retailers. It's worth noting that both Target and Microsoft are currently sold out, which could be what Sharma was referring to in her comments about supply not being able to keep up with demand.
Xbox Series X (All-Digital Edition)

We’ve seen a lot of evidence over the years suggesting Xbox console sales are lagging badly behind PS5. The most recent hint that this is the case came from Capcom, which says only 8.6% of Resident Evil Requiem sales were on Xbox . But if you’re willing to throw in with Microsoft anyway, you can get an Xbox Series X at MSRP at most of the usual retailers, with the exception of Xbox directly.
Xbox Series S (512GB)
The slightly less powerful Xbox Series S is available in two models that are identical in all ways except the amount of storage that comes in them.
Xbox Series S (1TB)
The same goes for the digital-only (and less powerful) Xbox Series S. It’s available at MSRP pretty much everywhere consoles are sold.
What About Nintendo Switch 2

Nintendo seems to have plenty of Switch 2 consoles on hand, but if you’re curious about how much it costs and where to get it, you can check out the links above. Like PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, it’s widely available at MSRP.

With all that said, if you’re considering picking a new game console this holiday season, you may want to do it sooner rather than later. It’s absolutely quite possible that Sony and Microsoft are simply looking ahead at the Black Friday sales rush when issuing their warnings about stock. It’s possible a bunch of GTA 6 fans will rush out to get a console when the game launches on November 19 (preloads start November 10, by the way).

And it’s looking like RAMageddon will only get worse in 2027 , meaning we could see further console shortages or price increases in the near future. So grab a console if you need it, because they’re readily available at the time of this writing.

content.v: 近日外媒comicbook编辑发文称，《 影之刃零 》的战斗满足感不只来自提高难度。流畅动画、招架反馈以及武器与“幻刃”的切换，共同构成了富于变化的战斗节奏，让玩家能够尝试不同招式组合。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261101/1793499276_258949_jpg_r.jpg
在该编辑的体验中，玩家不必始终采用最安全的生存方案，也可以把普通遭遇打成一场武术表演。不过，强调战斗表现力并不意味着取消技术要求：识别敌人动作、寻找空当并判断出手时机仍需技巧，掌握系统后也会获得明确回报。
相比依靠反复背诵首领招式取胜，编辑更愿意记住完成精彩操作的战斗。随着玩家逐渐熟悉系统，角色会显得更强，操作也会更加精准，这种成长构成了另一种满足感。
该编辑在体验“地狱行者”难度后仍希望获得更高挑战，但认为个人对难度的偏好不应掩盖游戏已经展现出的战斗表现力。相关判断来自个人体验和类型观点，并非对难度平衡或最终品质的客观定论。

content.v: 一项针对Steam产品说明的社区分析显示，2026年10月在该平台发行的新作中，49.9%披露使用了AI生成内容。2025年同期这一比例为26.4%，最新数据已接近前一年同期的两倍。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261104/1793737259_816278_jpg_r.jpg
同一分析列出的2024年1月数据仅为1.7%，由此反映出的披露比例在两年多时间里明显上升。不过，统计对象是产品说明中带有AI使用声明的新作，并非经过独立检测、确认使用AI的全部游戏。
材料称，披露使用AI的作品主要是规模较小的游戏，大型高预算作品目前仍以人工制作为主。相关技术也可能仅被用于临时纹理等辅助开发环节，因此披露AI内容并不意味着整款游戏完全由AI制作。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261104/1793737261_907825_jpg_r.jpg

content.v: 近日滨口直树表示，《 最终幻想7：重制版 》是重制三部曲中最难开发的一作。困难并非来自作品规模，而是团队需要在制作游戏的同时，从零建立开发组织和工作体制。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261104/1793737187_567834_jpg_r.jpg
滨口回顾称，项目重启之初只有约30名开发人员。团队既要扩充人员、完善组织，也要推进游戏开发，相当于一边制作首作，一边搭建支撑整套三部曲的制作体系。
首作还承担了确立系列基础标准的任务。团队需要决定画面、游戏体验和整体品质应达到何种程度，其中最难判断的是怎样的质量水平才能满足玩家期待。
这些基础工作完成后，后续两部作品便可沿用已有框架继续扩展和改进。因此，作品规模更大并不必然代表开发过程更加困难。滨口的判断主要针对团队和制作体系的创建成本，并非对三部作品的内容规模或最终品质进行排序。
《最终幻想7：重制版》由野村哲也担任主要导演，滨口直树与鸟山求担任联合导演；滨口此后负责后续作品。

items.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever just received a massive batch of class-balance updates ahead of launch that have bo

content.v: World of Warcraft: Forever just received a massive batch of class-balance updates ahead of launch that have boosted power across the board, but one group of players isn't happy with the changes: Shamans.

Developer Blizzard recently released Forever's launch patch notes based on feedback and data accumulated during the beta, resulting in a power spike for all classes and major reworks for classes like Paladin and Rogue. Shamans, too, received some significant changes, most notably the removal of a key Elemental specialization ability, Lava Burst, along with any interactions other abilities had with it.

It's that change, and other changes to specialization-specific abilities like Restoration's Riptide and Enhancement's Maelstrom Weapon, that have resulted in the WoW Classic Shaman Discord going into lockdown in protest. The entire server, which has around 80,000 members, has been made read-only, with a message declaring the reason for why it took what it described as such a "drastic measure."

"Community feedback gets completely ignored and class fantasies are getting destroyed," the server declared. "With this we intend to give them [Blizzard] a sign and show them that the community is not [happy] with how they approached our beloved class. Give us back our class and spec identities and fantasies."

While the protest is in regards to class changes in Forever specifically, the server is also home to Shaman discussions as they relate to other "classic" versions of the game as well, including WoW Classic and Mists of Pandaria Classic. As of writing, all of those channels are also locked and set to read-only.

In a follow-up post, the server went into more detail about its complaints in regards to how Blizzard has approached Forever's Shaman design. It stated its complaints aren't about "damage output." It also made clear the server will re-open "regardless of the outcome," but that it felt like its feedback through "legitimate" channels were being ignored.

The server then proceeded to list what it viewed as wrong with various ability changes for each Shaman specialization. It additionally called attention to what it called the "hybrid spell power issue," where spell power and intellect gear seems to be better for not only Elemental but also Enhancement, muddying the identity between the two specializations.

Blizzard has previously said it doesn't want "hybrid" classes that can deal damage and heal, like Shamans, to deal more damage than dedicated DPS classes. Players in the WoW community refer to this idea as the "hybrid tax," something those running the Shaman Discord said they are fine with if it means Shaman class design is improved.
"Truthfully, hybrid tax us all you want if the result is a cohesive class with strong class fantasy elements that are actually represented in our playstyles," it said.

This isn't the first time a WoW class Discord shut down in protest of how class changes. As pointed out by Wowhead , back in August 2025, the modern WoW Paladin Discord was partially closed in protest of the Retribution specialization's raid performance. In that case, only Retribution-specific channels were locked, and the entire protest lasted less than 24 hours. Blizzard did announce Retribution Paladin buffs shortly after, though it's unclear if those changes came at least in part due to the server protest or not.

How long the WoW Classic Shaman Discord remains in lockdown remains to be seen, but Forever launches November 4. Blizzard recently said it doesn't expect to make any more major class changes for at least another month .

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/cTeZTtGXV6uYdPks5D77R7-1920-80.png

Welcome to FOV 90, an FPS column from staff writer Morgan Park. Every other week, I cover topics relevant to first-person shooter enjoyers, spanning everything from multiplayer and singleplayer to the old and the new.

Welcome back to a special election day edition of FOV 90, the only FPS column that insists American readers vote twice today —first on important videogame matters right here, then on crucial *gestures at everything else* matters at your designated polling place .

items.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is gearing up for launch with some major class balance changes , but don't expect a

content.v: World of Warcraft: Forever is gearing up for launch with some major class balance changes , but don't expect any more for at least a month.

As detailed in Forever's launch patch notes , Blizzard is making some dramatic class changes, including major reworks to Rogue and Paladin talents, in time for release that will result in a big spike in player power. Blizzard said it has used all the data from the game's month-long beta to "get everything tuned to a reasonable place."
However, don't expect additional changes in the near future. Blizzard said it won't be making significant balance changes until sometime next month.

"With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don't plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month," Blizzard wrote in its patch notes. "Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data."
Forever's three launch raids will open December 9, meaning there will be a little over a month without class changes. But launch and its subsequent months will just be the beginning, Blizzard said.

"This is all merely a starting point for the classes in Forever, which will continue over the course of the months and years ahead just as they did following the original launch in 2004," Blizzard said.

Blizzard is in it for the long haul with Forever, telling GameSpot in an interview it hopes the game will continue to receive updates for the next 10-20 years (or potentially forever). It recently announced its plans to release major Forever content updates every four months , as well as teased how its controller support will eventually lead to players being able to play the MMORPG on "whatever you want."

WoW: Forever launches November 4, but you can make your character now . In other Forever news, Blizzards revealed it will be making major improvements to the game's divisive layering system , how it's avoiding the problem of "dead" servers , and announced big changes to racial abilities alongside its newly announced class changes.

content.v: Rockstar Games has confirmed more details about Grand Theft Auto 6 's impending release on November 19, including more information about physical goodies. content.v: You might be thinking, if you're the optimistic sort, that today's official unveiling of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel means that wheels are turning and things are happening and you're going to be off to Hammerfell soon —or at the very least, learning more about what's coming in Bethesda's next big RPG. Alas, in a follow-up post on social media, the studio made it clear that you shouldn't start holding your breath just yet.

"Thank you for 40 years of shared memories," Bethesda wrote. "We can't wait to make even more together with The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Development continues, and while it'll be some time before we're ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you."

Thank you for 40 years of shared memories. We can’t wait to make even more together with The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Development continues, and while it’ll be some time before we’re ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you.

"Some time" is obviously not a defined span, but I find that generally speaking it's a nicer, more politic way of saying "long time"—for instance, you could say it's been "some time" since Bethesda first announced the Elder Scrolls 6, and yeah, that's true. It was also eight freakin' years ago , and we've heard basically nothing since.

That is, very roughly, the same amount of time Bethesda needed to make the first Elder Scrolls game, Arena, as well as Daggerfall, Morrowind, the Morrowind expansions Tribunal and Bloodmoon, and the spinoff games Battlespire and Redguard. If you're (relatively) new to the series, eight years represents the span between Oblivion and The Elder Scrolls Online, a stretch interspersed by Skyrim and five major expansions: Knights of the Nine and Shivering Isles for Oblivion, and Dawnguard, Hearthfire, and Dragonborn for Skyrim.

Of course, Bethesda's had other things on the go over the past eight years too. Todd Howard said shortly after The Elder Scrolls 6 reveal that it was in pre-production , while Starfield was in full production. Starfield was Bethesda's top priority in the years leading up to its 2023 release; Howard later said that they'd just wanted to answer the fan question ( are you making a new Elder Scrolls? ) that came up every time they announced something else, like Starfield.

"Just pretend we didn't announce it," he joked. "Doesn't exist. No one's heard a word." How long Sentinel will take to get from here to launch is anybody's guess, although Bloomberg's Jason Schreier said on Bluesky that it's "still more than two years away." When questioned about his prediction, Schreier asserted that it's not a prediction at all, and that he knows "the time frame the game is targeting."

items.title: Xbox 制作了鳄鱼形状的 Series X，你可以在 GTA 6 发布之前赢得它
items.summary: GTA 6 is mere weeks away from launch, and to celebrate, Xbox is bringing the wildlife of Leonida to players’ l

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/03/xbox-series-x-bite-alligator-console-sweepstakes-1793733499952.jpg
GTA 6 is mere weeks away from launch, and to celebrate, Xbox is bringing the wildlife of Leonida to players’ living rooms with a one-of-a-kind console.

The Xbox Series X-Bite, as it’s been affectionately dubbed by the company, is a 5-foot-long, alligator-shaped, fully functional Xbox Series X. It’s quite convincing, actually, and it even looks like a piece of genuine taxidermy. Thankfully, that’s not the case; this life-sized fake alligator was created in partnership with John Nolan Studio, which created special effects for Netflix’s The Witcher series, Jurassic World Dominion , and HBO’s upcoming Harry Potter show.

To turn on the console, simply push the Xbox button on the gator’s back; it’s got a controller placed carefully in its jaws, bearing tooth marks as proof of its ravenous appetite. Even the pupils in its eyes are shaped like an X, outlined in green in keeping with Xbox branding.

This strange blend of technology and artwork isn’t an avante-garde installation sitting in the Microsoft corporate offices; starting today, November 3, fans can enter a sweepstakes to win the quirky console for themselves. Here’s how to participate:

The sweepstakes lasts until 11:59pm PT on November 10, 2026. The lucky winner will have 48 hours to claim the console; if they fail to do so, the gator will “make a clean getaway.” Additionally, the sweepstakes is only open to legal residents of the 50 U.S. and D.C. who are 18 years of age or older.

While Xbox didn’t directly mention GTA 6 in its posts about this unique contest, it’s hard not to see why it was made; the game takes place in a fictional version of Florida, which, as most folks will know, is home to all sorts of critters, including alligators. (It’s unclear if players will be able to wrassle gators bare-handed like they do in real-life Florida, but we figure the X-Bite is the next best thing.)

GTA 6 launches on November 19 on PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X|S. (Or the X-Bite.) Just this morning, its install size and global release times were revealed, with preload dates also confirmed for November 9 and 10.

Given that the file size is 212 GB, Rockstar has urged players to preload the game on their consoles as soon as they can. “Make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible,” Rockstar said on the game’s official website.

Fans are more keen than ever to get their hands on a copy of GTA 6, to the point where oodles of IGN’s readers are actually calling out of work to play it . A separate survey from Unwind Media even shared some concerning statistics that showed a baffling amount of players are so desperate to play the game early that they would even give up their pets if that meant they could experience it a week before launch.

items.title: 《魔兽世界：永恒》发布后将给玩家带来巨大的伤害提升
items.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is changing in some major ways for launch, with Blizzard revealing classes across t

content.v: World of Warcraft: Forever is changing in some major ways for launch, with Blizzard revealing classes across the board will deal more damage as it pursues design solutions that better fit in with Forever's combat.

In a lengthy developer note attached to Forever's launch patch notes , Blizzard outlined its philosophy for its latest version of WoW. It said during the game's nearly month-long beta that it was trying to keep player power in check. That meant every time it gave a class new tools and abilities, it had to tone down others to compensate. Blizzard now thinks that was the wrong approach.

"Those reductions left some iconic abilities feeling lackluster, and closed the door to other potentially exciting design options," Blizzard said. "So over the last two weeks, we've raised damage on classes across the game, and have increased the health of higher-level creatures to compensate."

In addition to classes simply doing more damage, classes themselves are changing in major ways. Elemental Shamans, for example, have had Lava Burst, a key part of their class during the beta, removed entirely. It's an example of what Blizzard said was the developer hastily "turning to Burning Crusade or Wrath-era solutions" rather than creating new ideas for how classes should play in Forever compared to previous versions of WoW.

"Our aim in class design is not perfect numerical equality, but rather for every class to feel valuable to groups they join, with powerful, unforgettable moments brought on by mastering them," Blizzard said. "In Forever this is accomplished by doubling down on the strengths and differences that make each class unique, rather than overly unifying them."

Alongside Shaman, a number of other classes have received significant changes going into launch, particularly Paladin and Rogue, with much of their talent trees almost completely reworked. Every class has received some balance changes.

Though the patch notes are largely dedicated to class changes, there are some other adjustments coming for launch as well. There are a number of tweaks to the game's controller support and bug fixes for various quests. Blizzard stated it additionally increased enemy respawn rates in the world for launch, particularly in lower-level zones. Its goal isn't to completely remove contention for spawns but to make it so players aren't hitting hard bottlenecks.
"Once the initial launch surge of low-level characters has settled down, we will adjust the lower-level zones down to more typical rates," Blizzard said.

items.title: Bethesda 的第一位全职 QA 测试员通过极其冷静的态度获得了这份工作
items.summary: It was a simpler time.

content.v: This week, Bethesda Game Studios is celebrating its 40th birthday—a celebration that included the full name reveal of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel , successfully completing the eight-year task of adding a word to a thing.

In addition, Bethesda is commemorating the occasion with the launch of a 40th anniversary site collecting the anecdotes and favorite memories of studio staff, including one Alan Nanes. Now a design director, Nanes was originally hired at Bethesda as one of its first full-time QA testers—and by his own description, he got the job by being a pleasant fellow to spend time with.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/8Cs2LdUoSYndUiKdaU3hXc-1920-80.jpg

According to Nanes, his history with Bethesda started during Morrowind's development. He was close friends with Bethesda devs in multiple departments, and it was an era where that was enough to get you in the building.

"Things were a bit 'Wild West' back then, and my friends allowed me to hang out (yes, before I was an employee) there, playing multiplayer games with them and just getting to know everyone," Nanes wrote. "Eventually, Todd Howard noticed my presence in the studio and asked if I wanted to test out their new game."

In time, his impromptu testing sessions started attracting an audience of Bethesda developers who would pick his brain about their design choices, scribble notes, and debate with each other about potential tweaks to the game while watching over his shoulder.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/JmF4o6RuMPxHWWr64cRf5N-1920-80.jpg

"It was an extraordinary feeling, the first time I felt like I was contributing to the creation of an actual videogame (I believe you can find my name in the Morrowind manual's credits under 'Special Thanks')," Nanes said. "After this became a regular occurrence, Todd Howard and Ashley Cheng seemed to decide having full-time, in-studio QA would be a valuable addition to the team, and I took on that mantle."

Nanes later graduated to a quest designer position for Oblivion, and was more recently credited as lead companions designer on Starfield. But while his tenure at Bethesda might've had a storybook trajectory, the history of QA workers at the studio has been a contentious one in the years since Nanes was hired.

Driven by frustrations surrounding compensation, advancement opportunities, workload, and more, QA workers at Bethesda's parent company ZeniMax initiated a unionization vote in 2022, officially forming ZeniMax Workers United - CWA—then the largest videogame union in the US—when the vote succeeded in January 2023 .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/NLQUJwJ3b6qncSQtppie5h-1920-80.jpg

Those frustrations remained unaddressed as contract negotiations with Microsoft stalled for over two years, driving the QA union to vote overwhelmingly in favor of authorizing a strike in April 2025. Its contract was ultimately ratified in June 2025 . When a number of those QA workers were affected by Xbox's July 2026 layoffs , that contract allowed the union to enter into an "effects bargaining" process to negotiate severance terms for its impacted members, culminating in "a significant agreement" in September 2026.

items.title: “刚刚删除了几 TB 的 AI 垃圾”：Itch.io 反击其店面中的 AI 泛滥
items.summary: Itch.io has also expanded its AI filters, enabling users to exclude games made with different types of generat

content.v: Indie-oriented digital storefront Itch.io is beginning to push back against the rising flood of AI, announcing on social media that it's "deleted a couple terabytes of AI slop" and made it easier for users to filter out games made with generative AI.

A few days after Valve admitted that Steam has a problem with AI slop and game cloning , Itch.io chimed in to say it's experiencing something very similar: The number of game pages being created every day on the storefront has doubled over the past two months .

Itch.io didn't provide a reason for the phenomenon, but it's not hard to figure out: When one Bluesky asked why it was happening, Itch.io replied "take a guess," accompanied by crying and robot smilies, and then added that "the number of downloads and purchases has *not* doubled."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/8g2gGgjWkBNbH4vVHxbBkM-1920-80.png

Now it seems to be moving to action. "Just deleted a couple terabytes of AI slop," the storefront posted last night. "Just because you can upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models doesn't mean you should upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models."

The account also linked to Itch.io's guidelines on "uploading excessive amounts of automatically generated or AI-generated content," which says that while content created by generative AI "can be useful or interesting, do not use automated systems to mass produce product pages. We will consider this spam and may remove your pages from our browse and search pages."
The guidelines apply to, but are not limited to:

Like Steam, Itch.io requires developers and publishers to disclose their use of generative AI in their games. That disclosure requirement has now been expanded from game assets to "the tabletop (aka physical games), books, comics and soundtracks categories," all of which now require disclosure.
It has also added new browsing and search filters on the site, so users can exclude some or all use of generative AI.

The tabletop (aka physical games), books, comics and soundtracks categories on itchio now require completing an AI disclosure in order to edit or create your page. These join the game assets section which has required disclosure for the past 2 years.
The "No AI" tag page cuts straight to it:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/eYBviqnYD5Mgg6VtJPYUHY-1920-80.png

Itch.io's action isn't likely to stem the tide of AI slop that's engulfing the world of gaming. Apart from the fact that it represents a very small percentage of a market dominated by Steam, the simple truth is that AI slop is easy to churn out in overwhelming quantities—that's what makes it so attractive to people who care less about creation than they do about making a few bucks on a lucky swing of the bat.

But it is action, and I think that's important: While some argue that mandatory AI disclosures have the potential to harm developers, the gen AI geyser is unquestionably doing harm right now , to users, developers, and the industry as a whole. Unless and until that changes, proactively excising the worst of the slop torrent and making it easier for gamers to avoid the mess entirely is the least that online storefronts can do.

content.v: Konami might have finally set down the Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol 1 to focus on releasing Metal Gear Solid 4 from its PS3 prison, but modders continue chipping away at the PS2-and-earlier era Metal Gear games. MGSHDFix, whose mission statement is to repair broken visual bugs, fix crashes, and generally give the older Metal Gears a bit of a spitshine, has got a big new update. Now is the era of MGSHDFix 5.0 (actually, 5.0.1. There was a hotfix).

"We've got performance improvements, massive vanilla loading time reductions for MGS2, loose .MP3/.WAV/.OGG/FLAC soundtrack loading for MG1/MG2, WIP raw mouse input support, and loads of new restoration and bugfixes", writes author Afevis Solmunko.

There are, to be honest, way too many fixes to properly delve into here, so I recommend either checking the patch notes out yourself or taking the mod for a spin in your preferred Metal Gear. We can call out some of the big ones, though.

For example, want to play Metal Gear 2 as Mel Gibson? No? Well that's a shame, bucko, because MGSHDFix 5.0 provides an option to restore that game's MSX2 sprites. "Yes, you can finally experience Mel Gibson fighting Sean Connery as Kojima intended," writes Solmunko.
Also in the OG MGs, there's now an option "to make doors automatically check your inventory for keycards (how MGS2 keycards work)", which frankly sounds blasphemous to me.

More practically, the latest version of the mod boasts that it dramatically cuts down loading times in MGS2. "We've greatly sped up level loading by adding a new system that prefetches a list of all the assets for all the rooms that are directly connected to the current stage you're in… Speedrunners have reported that this new prefetch system has shaved upwards to 5 minutes off of the elapsed realtime from their runs". On Linux (and thus, Steam Deck) specifically, Solmunko says this can "reduce level transitions load times by 4~6 seconds for every room you go into".
Plus, MGS2 and MGS3 now have limited support for raw mouse input in third-person, with support for first-person hopefully coming in MGSHDFix 5.1.0.
All good news, in other words, and it's nice these classics are now released in a way that lets fans do this kind of loving work for as long as they like.

items.title: PlayStation Officially Announces Its First 2026 Black Friday Sale
items.summary: PlayStation has officially announced its upcoming Black Friday sale — but where are the console deals?

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/03/psblackfrday26-1-1793723614396.jpg

PlayStation has officially announced its upcoming 2026 Black Friday sale. Deals drop on PlayStation Direct at midnight on November 4, with the full sale running until November 30. This marks a significant shift from last year’s strategy, which limited discounts to the week of Black Friday proper.

As for what the deals will actually include? This year’s announcement is pretty slim on the details, simply noting that "you’ll find deep discounts up to 75% off, across thousands of PS5, PS4 and PS VR2 games, expansions, and DLC." You read that right — no mention of consoles, accessories, or even PS Plus memberships.
PlayStation’s 2026 Black Friday Sale Is All About the Games

The announcement offers a sneak peek at what games will go on sale, including some big new releases from 2026. We don't know exactly what the discounts will look like, but you can get a sense of each game by clicking through to IGN's original reviews:

Retailers like Best Buy and Amazon have already started dropping early Black Friday deals, where you’ll find even more discounts on older physical PS5 games like God of War Ragnarok and Ghost of Tsushima. Yes, the discs are a touchy subject , I know.
What About Everything Else?

It’s no secret that consoles are ridiculously expensive, so one would hope Black Friday would be the rare time you can get around the current MSRP. Unfortunately, it’s not looking good for PS5 deals in 2026.
Sony has traditionally announced a new PS5 game bundle for Black Friday, with last year’s being Fortnite-themed . This year? No mention of a bundle at all.

In 2025, Sony dropped a $100 discount across consoles , which pretty much cancelled out the PS5 price hike from the month before. In fact, last year Sony announced discounts across its entire hardware line, including $20 off DualSense controllers and $100 off the PSVR2.

This year’s announcement doesn’t include any indication of hardware discounts. That doesn’t mean the deals won’t exist, but it does suggest they won't be as good as last year, or perhaps even haven’t been settled on yet.
The one sign of hope? A little asterisk next to some sale dates.

The PlayStation announcement notes that some discounts will end on November 20 and be replaced with new offers. This date lines up with when Sony launched its full console deals last year, so there’s still a chance we see a 'second wave' of PlayStation Black Friday deals that actually includes some hardware.
Individual retailers like Best Buy or Amazon may also drop some kind of console discount, I just wouldn't expect it to be too hefty.
Sony Already Has Refurbished PS5 Deals

Not all hope is lost if you’re hoping to get your hands on a current-gen console, especially in the lead-up to perhaps the biggest console-exclusive release of all time. (GTA 6, in case that wasn’t clear.) It just might not be brand new.
Sony is currently offering $40 off refurbished PS5 bundles with DualSense controllers. The bundle starts at $518 for the Digital Edition , while the disc-drive model comes to $568 .

If you're looking for some extra cash to spend on Black Friday, Sony is offering up to $400 to anyone willing to offload their PS5 console and controllers. It seems we’re in full refurb territory, which likely stems from ongoing stock issues amid RAMageddon .

items.title: 《魔兽世界》的 D&D 交叉很简洁，但不一致——一页上很新颖，然后在下一页上耸耸肩指着你已经拥有的 PHB
items.summary: What's old is new again.

content.v: World of Warcraft's big crossover with Dungeons & Dragons is finally here—and despite being a huge flagship collaboration, one of the biggest MMOs meeting with one of the biggest TTRPGs, I'm sad to say I'm feeling just a touch whelmed. This sourcebook is inconsistent—filled with very cool character options in some places, and just pointing at the already-existing player's handbook in others.
That inconsistency doesn't let the whole project down, mind. There are still some rules tucked away in here that I think are great additions to any campaign, not just a World of Warcraft-themed one.

Let's start with the big one: Classes. WoW and D&D do have a lot of overlap in terms of class fantasy—there's not much in the way of appreciable differences between a Fighter and a Warrior, other than a few iconic abilities being missing from the pack. As a result, this rulebook essentially uses the pre-existing classes as a template to throw some WoW flavour on.

Some of these changes are meaningful—take, for example, the Death Knight. This uses the Paladin's chassis, but throws in a ton of impactful changes, replacing Lay on Hands with Death Coil, for example. It also throws a whole new raft of Death Knight-adjacent spells, adjusts your Find Steed with a cool undead ghost that can phase through objects, and more.

A lot of the classes are solved by custom spells like this—the Paladin, for instance, has just the one new subclass to cover for Holy and a bunch of iconic Paladin spells. But the balance of these is a touch skewiff in places. Take Divine Shield, for instance. This thing is straight busted.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ygmKsVst6kYvRmytKZk2mE-1920-80.png

It's a 4th level spell, which does admittedly mean you'll only get it at levels 13 plus, but it makes you immune to not only the damage of a triggering attack, but also all damage until the start of your next turn. AND you can't be moved or have your speed reduced. While absolutely correct for the flavour of WoW's iconic bubble, this is crazy overpowered.

And while some of these classes do have a lot new on offer, others are so thin on content it's a wonder why they're there at all. The rogue gets a particularly short end of the stick, for instance. Outlaw rogues are just given a reskinned version of 5e's Swashbuckler subclass (which does, in fairness, have some new Cunning Strike options to bring it up to parity). Otherwise, the book just points you in the direction of pre-existing subclasses.

Others are a complete miss, too. Shamans are all awkwardly stuffed into the chassis of the Barbarian, which only really works for Enhancement shamans—Elemental and Restoration shamans are pretty much just your standard D&D barbarian with some flavour-adjacent rage options, rather than the full spellcasters they are in the videogame.

This inconsistency in quality applies to character origins, too. Some of them have fully bespoke traits—Dracthyr get their visage forms, Void Elves get this cool void form that triggers when you hit identical numbers on an Advantage/Disadvantage roll, and so on. And then there are Orcs and Dwarves, some of WoW's most iconic races, where the book goes: Just use the stuff that's already in the PHB.

And yet, there's a lot to this supplement I actually like. When it's actually adding new options to the classes, I think they're cool—the Frost Mage flavoured feat, Fingers of Frost, gives you extra cold damage against restrained creatures, for example. But the real thing I would encourage you to just crib for your non-Azerothian games are its gathering and crafting systems.
Crafty rules

In 5e (and the 2024 rules), crafting's always been sort of a joke. There are tool proficiencies, but they might come up every once in a blue moon. The actual Player's Handbook just says to half the cost of an item, then smacks you around the head with a massive downtime cost for anything particularly expensive—a suit of plate armor takes a whopping 150 days to craft (though you can split this with extra help). At which point you might as well just eat the GP cost and buy the damn thing.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YgEeif9p6QZJ8SfR7HkmHN-1920-80.png

This book, however, has some really neat rules for gathering and crafting professions. Having the right tool proficiency gives you access to a profession, which you can level up when your proficiency bonus increases to new tiers (which also increases the rarity of the items you can make).

Instead of making players shell out the gold cost, these gathering professions have a neat little table for getting enough golds' worth in raw materials to make the thing, with extra bonuses for beating the involved DC by five or more. When you get to higher levels, certain recipes might require items from specific regions—and you might only know how to make those items via recipes obtained from certain factions.

It's still all pretty lightweight (although each profession does have a useful list of suggested recipes it should know) but that's honestly a boon to this system, rather than a bane, because you could very easily just slot this whole mechanic into your homebrew campaign with very little trouble.

And, more to the point, you could very easily make entire adventure hooks out of going to get specific materials for a recipe here—which helps solve D&D crafting's main issue: It's not relevant unless you have literal months of in-game downtime to kill. While the book doesn't make changes to the time-to-craft issue, it's still a major step up.
The fact that there's plenty to like in this book makes it all the more frustrating that it's so inconsistent."

Renown's another mechanic I like. You get renown with certain factions based on your origins, but you can increase this renown through play to get certain perks. For instance, improved renown with Darnassus gives you the option to learn certain proficiencies, gain a blessing from its leaders, or gather extra materials with herbalism. My favorite of these is the gnomeregan Shield Guardian perk, which specifically states that if you dip below 50 renown again, the guardian turns on you. Sorry buddy, my creator says you dropped off.

Aside from these rules additions, there are also some solid dungeon adventures with their own bespoke stat blocks, extra magic items, and a respectable bestiary full of critters to toss into your campaign.

The fact that there's plenty to like in this book makes it all the more frustrating that it's so inconsistent—some areas have novel, if a little wonky, additions to the system. Others shrug like the book's designers simply ran out of time and budget, pointing towards resources that you already own.

However, if you are looking to run a WoW-specific campaign, or just want crafting rules that don't suck, it very well might be worth checking out on the strength of its secondary mechanics alone. Just don't go in there expecting a 1:1 replication of the MMORPG. This is still Dungeons & Dragons—and in some places, I mean that literally.

items.title: 哨兵是什么意思？巨型机器人参与其中吗？上古卷轴 6：哨兵传说解释
items.summary: What does Sentinel mean? How is it connected to Skyrim? Are we getting giant robots? Here's a deep dive lore e

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/03/celebrating-40-years-of-bethesda-game-studios-7-46-screenshot-1793718533009.png

The worst-kept secret in gaming has finally been confirmed: yes, The Elder Scrolls 6 has a title. It’s called Sentinel, and will take place in Hammerfell, the province of northwest Tamriel previously featured in Daggerfall and Elder Scrolls Online (also Arena, but anyone who says they played that recently is lying). The point is, more than any previous mainline entry in the Elder Scrolls series, Sentinel will be depicting a fairly well-trodden location. But given its geographical location and significance in The Lore, I think there’s a fairly good chance that TES 6 will feature two distinct elements: ships and giant robots. Stay with me on this.

So what is Sentinel? Well, it’s a city and kingdom – think New York, New York – on the southern shores of the Iliac Bay, the northern edge of Hammerfell province, stretching from the Alik'r Desert and coastal regions in the west to the Dragontail Mountains in the east.

It’s a hugely important maritime city in Tamrielic lore, being the founding settlement of the Redguards. Its geography and architecture are heavily inspired by North Africa and the Middle East: the city of Sentinel is often depicted almost like classical Baghdad, with its beautiful domed palace and spires in the centre, river canals lined with palm trees, and sandblasted common districts full of markets and street vendors. It is one of the preeminent locations of TheElder Scrolls 2: Daggerfall, second only perhaps to Daggerfall itself, its opposite number and historical rival across the water. Like Rome and Carthage squabbling over Sicily, Sentinel and Daggerfall’s shared past mostly pivots around a dispute over the island of Betony, a strategically significant fishing community off the coast of High Rock which used to be a protectorate of Sentinel until Daggerfall decided to sink their navy over it.

It’s a region rich with naval tradition, arguably with lots of parallels to the Mediterranean. The northern province of High Rock may be taken as a composite of Latin and Germanic Europe as a counterpart to Sentinel’s obvious riffs on the Arab-descended Moorish people who once colonised the Iberian Peninsula. Which is fitting, because if Elder Scrolls is anything, it’s extremely moreish.

What’s important is that the Iliac Bay is full of tiny islands. The lore is steeped in boat stuff. The Redguards themselves are a seafaring people in the same way that Bretons are a magic one, or that the Imperials are really good at accountancy: it’s at the heart of their culture, their DNA. Which, given that Sentinel is named for their home nation, would seem to track with the rumour from several billion years ago that The Elder Scrolls 6 would feature, or at least was once intended to feature, some sort of ship-based component. That could mean anything or nothing, of course, but if every Elder Scrolls game is to be its own proposition, then this would certainly be a defining trope for the new one. Skyrim had dragons. Oblivion had portals to hell. Morrowind had big mushrooms. Yum.

Beyond the bay itself, we have the fallen continent of Yokuda, where the Redguards originally hail from, and the large island nation of Stros M’Kai, the setting of Bethesda’s one-time experiment in doing a third-person adventure spin-off of the Elder Scrolls. The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard wasn’t a huge success in itself, but it did teach the studio a great deal about the relationship between scale and hand-crafted detail that resulted in a massive difference in approach between Daggerfall and Morrowind. Where the former boasted a map twice the size of the UK, Morrowind crammed infinitely more intrigue into a region barely a full percentage of the size, brought the series to consoles, and subsequently made the studio a household name.

Bethesda would stick to this philosophy of staunchly hand-crafted worlds until Starfield, which depicted a thousand-planet galaxy of endless walking, pocked with procedurally generated identikit outposts and very little incentive to go off the laid-out path, which many would argue – myself included, and I like Starfield – betrayed a studio that had lost touch with its core appeal. But think of the parts of Starfield which are successful, at least as a proof of concept: a mobile home in the form of a starship, to which you can assign crew, and go adventuring with them. A hugely popular ship builder that simplified the process of pimping your ride down to a snap-together kitbash, that allowed for enormous creativity within a deceptively rigid framework.

It’s not a given that any of this will be relevant to Sentinel, or that if any of these systems carried over they would retain their complexity. But it does demonstrate that, if TES 6 were to think about this sort of direction, it’s hardly unprecedented at this point.

What’s also not unprecedented in Bethesda’s oeuvre is kaiju. Big bastards smashing the gaffe up. Some years before Fallout 3’s Liberty Prime made us all piss ourselves unintentionally, the end of Oblivion depicted daedric prince Mehrunes Dagon ransacking the Imperial City, and you’ll probably remember that he’s a big dude, so big that he could only be seen off by the literal embodiment of Akatosh as a nine-storey dragon. And yes, the dragons of Skyrim qualify: the entire game being built around the proposition of seeing off a veritable invasion of enormous, scaly bastards. And Morrowind before them was all about preventing Dagoth Ur from building a second Numidium with which to conquer the world: a gigantic Dwarven mech powered by the literal heart of a god, based on the schematics of a weapon of mass destruction that was once used by the city-state of Sentinel to conquer the rest of the region.

And there’s a whole other bunch of stuff that happened: if you want to know more, boot up Morrowind, or Oblivion, or Skyrim, and read an in-game book entitled The Warp in the West, which explains a convoluted collision of realities in which every rival faction got to use Numidium to get their preferred Daggerfall ending, making all of them canon at once. Which you might call a cop-out, but it certainly neatly solves the kinds of insurmountable issues that crop up when you try to respect all player choices.

The point is this: after the events of Daggerfall, Numidium is destroyed, and pieces of it are scattered all over Hammerfell and High Rock. Perhaps some of it sank to the bottom of the bay. Perhaps some of it is buried in the desert. The quote displayed at the end of the recent Sentinel teaser talks about the experience of Yazar, a Moth Priest, trying to interpret a prophecy from one of the Elder Scrolls and receiving only a faint image of some kind of terrible future. Or past. Or parallel present. “A future lost, a victory undone, sands of time scattered by fate”.

Like much of Elder Scrolls lore, it is esoteric and steeped in double-meaning. As a region at the heart of the Warp in the West, the ‘sands of time’ could well refer literally to the Alik'r Desert while caught in a time-warp. A ‘victory undone’ may refer to any number of conflicts referenced in the series’ history, but the most pertinent one would seem to be Sentinel’s “victory” at the end of Daggerfall, in which it became the capital of a vast coastal region as the various bickering city-states and territories were consolidated into the four currently standing kingdoms of the Iliac Bay, which, along with Sentinel, includes the Breton kingdoms of Daggerfall and Wayrest, and the Orcish kingdom of Orsinium.

items.title: 《魔兽世界》永远发布补丁说明带来控制器支持和大规模职业变更
items.summary: World of Warcraft Forever is just a day away, and now that the beta has concluded Blizzard has released its pa

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/28/wow-1790594365869.jpg
World of Warcraft Forever is just a day away, and now that the beta has concluded Blizzard has released its patch notes for the release build of the game.

A bulk of the patch notes focus on class changes where, among other things, Blizzard rolled back some Shaman abilities like Lava Burst to focus the Elemental spec identity on lightning ability. And that's just one of dozens of class changes. Blizzard's goal with these class changes was to distill Forever's combat into its own identity. According to the developer notes, "some of this round of changes reflects areas where we were likely hasty in turning to Burning Crusade- or Wrath-era solutions rather than carving out new ones that better fit into the Forever combat model."

This will likely be the only major class tuning that Blizzard is going to touch before raids open next month, which is perfectly in line with how the company typically launches WoW games and expansions. The developers want to gather data on how people are playing before it changes how anything is balanced, which only makes sense.

However, Blizzard will still tweak classes to fix bugs, according to the developer notes. "With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don’t plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month," the developer said. "Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data."

But apart from the mass of class changes, World of Warcraft Forever's controller support has "entered a complete functional state," and gamepads can now be used in every facet of the MMO. Xbox even put out its own blog post talking about Forever's controller support , claiming that it "reimagines the way we play." WoW Forever's beta supported controllers, but that support was only in an alpha stage, and had its own limitations and bugs. Hopefully this "complete functional state" means Blizzard has figured those issues out.

I, for one, plan to download WoW Forever on an Xbox Ally X , so that I can grind while I watch TV. But because Forever's controller UI looks so similar to Final Fantasy XIV's controller interface, I can't help but wonder if this controller support is just a precursor for a full Xbox Series X release. We'll just have to wait and see what happens there.

Finally, the patch notes do detail some nerfs coming to racial abilities. Dwarves and Orcs both straight up had one of their passive abilities removed from the game, while many other races had their passives nerfed. For instance, Humans' Ruthless ability now increases critical strike chance by 1%, rather than 2%. But, hey, at least Trolls get a longer duration on Berserking – their mini-bloodlust.

Only time will tell how balance is going to fall in WoW Forever, but we won't have to wait long to see how it plays out. World of Warcraft Forever comes out tomorrow, November 4, at 3pm PST / 6pm EST , and if the beta was any indication, a lot of people are going to rush in to really push WoW's servers to their breaking point. And I'll be right there to watch it happen.

items.title: Xbox 25 年捆绑包包含所有这些游戏，售价 570 美元
items.summary: To celebrate the 25th anniversary of Xbox this year, Microsoft has launched a "25 Years of Xbox" digital game

content.v: To celebrate the 25th anniversary of Xbox this year, Microsoft has launched a "25 Years of Xbox" digital game bundle. It includes 25 games for $570.

That works out to about $23/game, but it's more nuanced than that, as some of the games are bundles themselves. For example, one of the games in the bundle, Halo: The Master Chief Collection, includes Halo 1, Halo 2, Halo 3, Halo 3: ODST, Halo: Reach, and Halo 4. There are Gears of War and Age of Empire bundles, too.
Some of the games in the bundle are for both Xbox and PC, and some are just for Xbox or just for PC. Additionally, many of the games in the pricy bundle are currently on Xbox Game Pass.
Given all of that, you may want to check your library and do some quick math before spending hundreds of dollars on this anniversary bundle.

2026 is the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and Microsoft wanted it to be a significant celebratory event for fans and employees alike, but the year has been terrible for the Xbox brand. After Microsoft named Asha Sharma the new Xbox CEO in February, she gutted Xbox as part of a "reset" that included mass layoffs, studio divestitures, and game cancellations. Sharma said these moves were necessary because Xbox was in such an unhealthy place in terms of its finances.

content.v: Yes, Aonuma knows how much you hate those Iron Boots.

It's no secret that Eiji Aonuma can see the issues with Ocarina of Time 's Water Temple. The series producer spoke about it when the game launched on 3DS, and it continues to haunt him today, as he's brought it up once again in the latest Ask the Developer interview.

"I had some overdue homework: I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago," Aonuma-san says of the Switch 2 remake. He touches on all the dungeon's much-discussed sticking points (the item menu annoyances, confusing layout, etc.), and confirms that he "had the team make some adjustments in this version".
